Dear all,

thank you for the discussion yesterday. I wanted to capture one possible way of structuring the Minecraft idea before we get too far into the autumn pilot.

Chris originally proposed an esports team and a path towards external competition. I think the limited pilot we have agreed can help us find out whether this could eventually become part of a broader Minecraft Education programme at the school, but I would not assume that wider programme at this stage.

One possible structure would be to use Minecraft Education for several related activities: the existing coding work, collaborative school-specific challenges, continued work on the RMIS campus world and, if the format proves useful, a more focused esports team.

In that model the autumn pilot would be the first practical cycle for testing the team and challenge format rather than the launch of a permanent school esports programme.

For the pilot itself I suggest we keep the current scope:

  • 14 participants;
  • after-school format;
  • internal team and challenge work;
  • coding and collaborative problem solving as part of the activities;
  • use of the RMIS Minecraft world where it is useful, without making completion of the world a requirement;
  • no dependency on an external competition during the first cycle.

The main reason for starting internally is that we still need to understand what works in the school environment. Before looking at external competition, it would be useful to see whether the team format works reliably, whether the challenge structure produces meaningful collaboration and coding activity, and what technical and organisational support is actually required.

If the pilot works well, we can then discuss whether there is enough interest and internal ownership to develop a broader programme or another cycle. That would still need a separate school decision.

I also agree with the idea of connecting some challenges to learning objectives. I would leave the exact themes open for now rather than designing the whole programme before we have learned from the pilot.

Best regards,
Daniel
